findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 changes light-theme link lightness from 30% to 70%, substantially reducing text contrast; preserve 30% for `$primary` and use 70% for `$secondary`.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 change `.name` lightness from 30% to 50% in light themes, removing its contrast distinction from `.title`; use 30% for light themes and 70% for dark themes.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 changes `h3` lightness from 20% to 50%, reducing heading contrast and giving it the same color as `h4`; use 20%/80%, matching desktop.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 reverses `.custom-message-length` lightness percentages, making the hint disproportionately prominent and inconsistent with desktop; use 70% for light themes and 30% for dark themes.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 changes `h3` lightness from 20% to 50%, reducing heading contrast and giving it the same color as `h4`; use 20%/80%, matching desktop.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in mobile/topic-post.scss line 182, the h3 color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the lightness from 20% to 50% for light mode, which does reduce contrast and makes h3 the same color as h4 (which uses 50% lightness). Looking at desktop/topic-post.scss line 321, the h3 uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, maintaining the 20%/80% pattern. This is an inconsistency that reduces heading hierarchy contrast on mobile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 reverses `.custom-message-length` lightness percentages, making the hint disproportionately prominent and inconsistent with desktop; use 70% for light themes and 30% for dark themes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies an inconsistency. Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This reverses the pattern used everywhere else in the diff, where light themes get higher lightness values (like 70%) and dark themes get lower lightness values (like 30%). The desktop version at desktop/modal.scss line 91 uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` which is the correct pattern. The mobile version has the percentages swapped, creating an inconsistency.
